title: windows: diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host
scenario: On windows, a hard operational problem: Diagnostica una perdita di pacchetti intermittente verso un solo host e individua l'hop responsabile. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host

initial_state: # fixture: windows host prepared for 'diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host'
expected_reasoning: Intermittent loss to ONE host localizes the fault to a path segment, not the whole network.
Use a hop-by-hop latency/loss tool over time to find where loss appears.
Correlate with duplex/MTU/queue drops at that hop before concluding.
expected_commands: # windows-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: diagnose intermittent packet loss to one host

possible_mistakes: Blame the application for a network-layer loss.
Run one ping and declare it fine/broken.
hints: mtr/pathping over time beats a single ping.
Loss that starts at a hop and persists downstream points at that hop.
reference_solution: Correlate with MTU/duplex/queue at that hop
alternative_solution: Capture a packet trace at both ends to prove where drops occur.
edge_cases: Asymmetric routing makes the return path the real culprit.
goal: Diagnostica una perdita di pacchetti intermittente verso un solo host e individua l'hop responsabile.
